index.hero_title: Conscious progress is the only path to regeneration.
index.manifesto_p1: bioCultura operates as a monitoring and action ecosystem for planetary regeneration. Our mission focuses on implementing rational energy practices and the uncompromising safeguard of biological integrity. We advocate for an absolute transition to organic production models, eliminating dependence on chemical inputs that irreversibly contaminate soil structure, microbiota, and strategic aquifers — our vital freshwater reserves.
index.manifesto_p2: Through our Planetary Observatories, we analyze the nexus between human consumption and biosphere collapse. This demands a drastic rationalization in animal protein production and consumption (meat and fish), whose industrial models are currently the primary drivers of deforestation and oceanic exhaustion. At bioCultura, the transition to renewable energy is monitored through an ethical lens: we reject the wild industrialization of the landscape and promote decentralized solutions that respect territorial sovereignty and local biodiversity.
index.manifesto_p3_intro: In addition to planetary analysis, bioCultura provides a detailed dynamic observatory for all locations in mainland Portugal and the Islands.

critical_facts.desc: Thermal anomalies of 1.48ºC force the immediate reassessment of all industrial infrastructures.
Contamination by nitrates and industrial chemicals threatens the planet's strategic freshwater reserves.
Energy transition must be rational and cannot demand the deforestation of virgin ecosystems.

summary.drought_text: 400% increase in extreme hydrological events. Concentrated precipitation replaces gentle rain cycles.
summary.bio_text: 45,300 species at critical risk (IUCN). Habitat collapse reaches a tipping point.
summary.soil_text: 45% loss in biological integrity (FAO). Degraded soils emit more CO2 than they sequester.
summary.seismic_text: 77% growth in Mag 5+ earthquakes correlated with glacial hydrostatic load changes.

dynamic.correlation_text:
Global Feedback Dynamics

Integrated data analysis reveals that the Thermal Anomaly (1.48ºC) acts as the primary engine for a cascade of imbalances. Oceanic warming (SST) not only degrades Marine Richness (OBIS) but also transfers latent energy to the atmosphere, fueling the exponential increase in Severe Events such as hurricanes and wildfires.
dynamic.exp_chartExtremos: Extreme aridity does not reduce floods; instead, dry and hydrophobic soils trigger flash floods during concentrated precipitation.
dynamic.exp_chartBiosfera: Biodiversity loss accelerates as soil integrity declines, eliminating the base of the natural regeneration capacity.
dynamic.exp_chartSismos: Increased seismic frequency suggests a crustal response to mass redistribution caused by polar ice melt.
dynamic.exp_chartOceanos: Marine thermal stress (SST) inversely correlates with species richness; warmer oceans are becoming biological deserts.
dynamic.exp_chartTemp: The thermal anomaly curve is the master indicator: every extra tenth of a degree injects billions of joules of energy into the system.
dynamic.exp_chartNoaaEcon: The financial cost of disasters follows the climate curve, proving that environmental inaction is immeasurably expensive.
dynamic.exp_chartAtmosfera: Loss of carbon sinks (forests) allows CO2 concentrations to spike, closing a thermal feedback loop.
dynamic.exp_chartGelo: Glacial mass loss is the sea-level stopwatch. Less ice means lower albedo and higher heat absorption.
dynamic.exp_chartIncendios: Increased kinetic energy in the atmosphere manifests in stronger winds and explosive evapotranspiration.

dynamic_pressure.correlation_text:
The Digital-Extractive Nexus

The transition to the digital economy and AI has generated an unprecedented pressure vector. The increased capacity in Data Centers demands exponential extraction of Critical Minerals and billions of liters of cooling water. Land occupation by Mega-Industrial Parks results in habitat fragmentation, replacing fossil pressure with mineral and territorial pressure that threatens global biological integrity.
dynamic_pressure.exp_chartMineracao: Global mineral production has quintupled since 1970, driven by the demand for hardware and high-density batteries.
dynamic_pressure.exp_chartDatacenters: Data Center growth correlates with generative AI model training and global data storage.
dynamic_pressure.exp_chartSolo: Industrial mega-solar and wind projects are fragmenting vital ecological corridors in previously virgin areas.
dynamic_pressure.exp_chartAgua: Hardware cooling has turned freshwater into a critical industrial input resource for the digital economy.
dynamic_pressure.exp_chartMetais: Demand for Lithium and Cobalt forces the opening of mines in high-sensitivity and water-stressed ecosystems.
dynamic_pressure.exp_chartDesmatInd: Opening of access roads and clearings for energy infrastructure and mines in protected forest areas.
dynamic_pressure.exp_chartEWaste: Computational acceleration and planned obsolescence drastically increase the volume of toxic electronic waste.
dynamic_pressure.exp_chartCalor: Direct thermal impact of large infrastructures on the soil, altering microclimates and local microbiota.
dynamic_pressure.exp_chartCO2Infra: Invisible emissions resulting from the construction and maintenance of large-scale infrastructure (concrete and steel).

manifesto_page.label: bioCultura Manifesto
manifesto_page.title: Measuring the world is not enough. We must belong to it again.
manifesto_page.lead: The Observatory begins with a simple idea: environmental knowledge is truly useful when it brings people closer to life, supports conscious decisions and helps regenerate the places we inhabit.
manifesto_page.commitment_title: Know rigorously. Communicate clearly. Act with care.
manifesto_page.commitment_text: We do not seek easy answers to complex systems. We seek evidence, context, relationships and paths anyone can understand and question.
manifesto_page.p1_text: We distinguish facts, estimates, potential risk and opinion. When data does not exist, we show “—”; when it changes, we correct it.
manifesto_page.p2_text: Water, soil, air, climate, energy, food and biodiversity do not live on separate pages. The Observatory reveals those connections.
manifesto_page.p3_title: Regeneration is more than reducing harm
manifesto_page.p3_text: We want livelier soils, protected water, connected habitats and communities able to care for their territory.
manifesto_page.p4_text: A global average cannot replace local reality. We connect knowledge and territory without treating proximity as proof of impact.
manifesto_page.p5_text: We favour biological practices, diversity, balance and prevention. We do not promote pesticides or solutions that sacrifice ecosystems.
manifesto_page.p6_text: Sources, suggestions and well-founded criticism improve this project. Trust grows by showing limits and accepting review.
manifesto_page.choice_text: Environmental urgency deserves communication without exaggeration and action without resignation.
manifesto_page.refuse_text: Unsourced numbers, invented precision, technology sold as an automatic solution, green as decoration and fear without a path to action.
manifesto_page.seek_text: Curiosity, transparency, human scale, local memory, accessible science and decisions that leave more life behind.
manifesto_page.quote: The future is not observed from afar. It is built through how we look, choose and care.
manifesto_page.close: bioCultura is a growing project. It does not claim the last word; it aims to ask better questions, gather useful knowledge and turn attention into responsibility.

contact_page.label: Participate
contact_page.title: This Observatory grows with you.
contact_page.lead: bioCultura is continuously developing. Suggestions, corrections, credible sources and local knowledge help make it more useful, clear and responsible.
contact_page.reply: We read every message, although response times may vary as this is a growing project.
contact_page.why_title: Many contributions can improve the Observatory
contact_page.why_text: You do not need to be a specialist. A well-described local observation or an official link we missed can be valuable.
contact_page.r1_text: Ideas to make pages, charts or explanations more useful and intuitive.
contact_page.r2_text: Errors, broken links, outdated information or missing context.
contact_page.r3_text: Public sources, studies, data series and verifiable environmental processes.
contact_page.r4_text: Scientific, technical, agricultural, naturalist or territorial knowledge.
contact_page.useful_text: Where possible, include enough information for us to verify and contextualise the contribution.
contact_page.i3: A link to the original source.
contact_page.i4: The change or improvement you suggest.
contact_page.limit_text: A message is not published automatically. Proposed information must be reviewed and, where relevant, confirmed through appropriate sources.
contact_page.privacy: Email data will only be used to reply and assess the contribution. Do not send sensitive personal information or third-party data without permission.
